threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of 'the underground.' Everyone knows it's a London thing, but you can't quite let go of that tourist vibe yet.
Last night on the 35, a guy in a suit was passionately singing Show Me Love. The bus driver just shook his head and smiled. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a kid sell homemade lemonade next to the Kottbusser Tor U-Bahn station while the BVG strike had everyone in chaos. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You ever notice how the BVG strikes always seem to happen right before the weekend? It's like clockwork. Guess they know how to keep us on our toes!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a real local when they roll their eyes at a BART delay but still have a backup plan involving a bike and some burritos.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Just saw a guy serenading the whole bus with a ukulele. Got off at 6th and Market, still humming the tune. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Most tourists think Gràcia is just a postcard. They miss the late-night chats over cheap wine in hidden squares, where locals laugh off the noise.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a newbie by how they still read the menu like a tourist; locals order tapas without hesitation and chat with the waiter.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newcomers; they're the ones still baffled by the weekend Tube closures and trying to navigate the bus routes on their phones.
Caught the N155 last night—two blokes arguing over who saw a ghost in the back. Got off with a voucher for a kebab after they made up.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw a group of kids playing with a disco ball in a park at noon, I knew I had found my home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Kreuzberg's spontaneous Kebab festivals showcase not just food, but a wild mix of art, music, and community that you won't find anywhere else.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only a true local knows that 'the cloud' isn't just about tech, but also about the fog rolling in and out of Dolores Park.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo at Larkin and Eddy, ready for a gala, but still waiting on a broken bus. Classic San Francisco—style meets struggle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think 'pancakes' at brunch means sweet, but locals dip theirs in omelette. Different food culture, but they never notice.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled by the Mercat de Gràcia's layout, trying to figure out which stall has the best jamón.
